ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A snail's horn supplies the minute ground for two recurrent corpus families.
EvidenceBody: In prose and verse, people contend for “the minuteness of a snail's horn,” and profit and fame on a fly's head and snail's horn become an empty battle. A discussion explicitly recalls the Zhuangzi story of Chu and Man fighting over territory and leaving corpses for ten thousand miles, then places even the yielding of Yao and Shun and the conquests of Tang and Wu in “the waste of the snail's horn.” Chan verses also reverse the scale: one puts the universe on the tip of a snail's horn, while a hall address opposes the passing traveler's labor over fly-head and snail-horn matters to a great treasure hidden in the body. The minute object, its contest language, and the vast things placed on it are one image under different predicates. The Chan deviation lies in bringing the horn into hall speech and scale-reversal verse, not in assigning it a hidden meaning. The exact phrase occurs 36 times in 26 allowlist texts.
